card: Removes ArgsManager wrapper functions in favor of calling std::optional::value_or directly. It eliminates boilerplate wrapper abstractions and removes the need for helper disambiguation code in pending settings refactors like PR #31260. The evidence is internal code simplification described by the author.
evidence: Decreases complexity at the foundation at the only cost of a change to ArgsManager::GetPathArg_() and slightly more verbose code in one leaf; src/qt/optionsmodel.cpp (author in PR description)
Also represents slight decrease in complexity of pending PR #31260 which has an extra GetPtr() function for disambiguating between overloaded functions (author in PR description)
problem: ArgsManager retains wrapper functions that add unnecessary layers over standard optional methods and create overload ambiguities that complicate other argument-handling refactors.

risk.why: Mistakes in fallback values when reading configuration options could cause settings to misread default values at startup or in the GUI.

scope_notes: Small mechanical cleanup touching ArgsManager internals and Qt optionsmodel.
summary: Removes wrapper helper functions in ArgsManager in favor of calling std::optional::value_or directly on retrieved settings. This simplifies the ArgsManager interface and updates call sites including ArgsManager::GetPathArg_() and optionsmodel.cpp.
